text: If you hid a hundred dollars under your bed in the year 2000, today it buys only half as much.
Nobody stole it. So where did the other half go?
In the river town, one basket of fish costs one golden egg.
Then the mayor finds a goose that lays golden eggs. And he hands them out to everyone.
Everyone feels rich. But the river still has the same fish.
So a basket costs two eggs. Then three.
The second man saved a hundred eggs in a jar. Now they buy a third of the fish.
The first man owes the lender fifty eggs. Now he pays it back with a few baskets.
The third man kept no eggs. He owns boats and nets. His fish just cost three eggs now.
The eggs didn't get stolen. There were just more of them.
That's inflation. In the last twelve months, American prices rose three point seven percent.
So where do you keep yours? In a jar, or in a boat?
